```typescript
import type { FreeCamera, SceneContext } from "@babylonjs/lite";
import { attachFreeControl } from "@babylonjs/lite";

export function attachBigWorldFly(camera: FreeCamera, canvas: HTMLCanvasElement, scene: SceneContext): () => void {
    const originalSpeed = camera.speed;
    camera.speed = originalSpeed * 20;
    const dispose = attachFreeControl(camera, canvas, scene);
    return () => {
        dispose();
        camera.speed = originalSpeed;
    };
}
```

1. Saves the original speed
2. Sets speed to 20x (making all keyboard movement 20x faster)
3. Attaches the library's free controls (keyboard + mouse)
4. Returns a dispose function that detaches the controls and restores the original speed

The mouse look is "exactly as the library's default" because:
- The drag-to-rotation mapping is the same (same angularSensitivity)
- The inertia decay is the same (same inertia value)
- The only difference is the stop threshold (speed * 0.001), which is 20x higher, meaning the coasting stops slightly sooner for very large drags
